C45224.observed: What was checked: whether the row tells you which bin the part will be pulled from, and whether that line only appears when there is something to say. What happened: choosing a stocked part put a line under the row reading "Pulled from" followed by a chip naming the bin - for the part tried, "Unassigned", which holds 6. With no part chosen from the catalogue - a description simply typed by hand - there is no allocation to make and the "Pulled from" line is not shown at all. So it appears exactly when there is an allocation and not otherwise.

C45240.observed: What was checked: what happens about bins when the part is typed in by hand rather than chosen from the catalogue. What happened: with "ZZAUTOTEST bins freetyped" typed in and a quantity of 2, no bin was allocated and no "Pulled from" chip appeared anywhere on the row. That is right - a part that is not linked to a catalogue part has no stock record to pull from, so there is nothing to allocate.

C45226.observed: What was checked: what happens when you click the "Pulled from" chip, and whether the list that opens gives you what you need to choose sensibly. What happened: clicking the chip opened a picker listing the bin the part is held in, showing its name "Unassigned", how many are on hand (6), a tick against the bin currently chosen, and a "Default" badge marking it as the default bin. The last item in the list is "Split across bins…", for spreading the quantity over more than one bin.
C45226.not_observed: This branch holds every stocked part in a single bin, so a list of several bins in catalogue order, and the warning styling on a bin that holds fewer than you asked for, could not be seen here.
